_doc: Single home of the orchestration thresholds. Hooks read this file; gate_policy.DEFAULT_PARAMS holds identical built-in defaults, so a missing or unreadable file changes no behaviour. Edit values here, not in code.
_doc_work_agents: Work agents are budgeted by context size and cumulative cost, never by tool-call count: a turn gets dearer only through context, and late turns are the productive ones.

call_caps._doc: Search/probe agents keep tool-call caps: their cost is the call, not the context. A type absent here and absent from work_agent_types is uncapped (watcher, currently).

_comment_poll_sleep_min_seconds: no-poll-gate: a `sleep` shorter than this many seconds paces requests and is allowed anywhere; this long or longer is polling and is refused in the foreground.
_comment_wait_for_limits: no-poll-gate: a subagent's foreground wait-for must pass --max <= wait_for_max_seconds and set a Bash timeout >= (--max + 30) s, at most bash_timeout_max_ms; a call reaching its timeout (default 120000 ms) is moved to the background by the harness.
_comment_skill_bytes_threshold: skill-load-gate: the main session is denied an expert skill whose SKILL.md (what the harness injects on load) exceeds this many bytes; an allowed load whose SKILL.md plus every *.md under the skill directory exceeds it gets both sizes as context.
_comment_override_reason_min_chars: Every override marker is a line `NAME: <reason>` (or `NAME="<reason>"`, optionally after `#`) with a reason of at least this many characters (gate_policy.override_marker).
_doc_main_only_skills: main-budget-gate: skills whose whole procedure runs in the main session by design; the budget gate does not count calls in a session that loaded one (skill-load-gate logs every allowed load).
_doc_process_skills: Process skills tell the main session how to run the loop, so the main session may load them at any size. Expert skills are loaded by the agent that does the work. Add a process skill by name in process_skills, or by naming convention in process_skill_globs (fnmatch patterns on the skill name) - no code edit either way.

spawn_rights._doc: Who may spawn whom, keyed by the type of the SPAWNING agent ('main' = the main session, which has no agent type). A list names the allowed types; "*" means everything the gate otherwise allows; {"allow": ..., "deny": {type: reason}} refuses the listed types with that reason; a type absent from this map gets the 'default' entry. Untyped requests (general-purpose/claude/empty) are refused for everyone. Escape hatch for both refusals, main session only: a spawn-prompt line `AGENT_TYPE_OVERRIDE: <reason>` (a reason is required). Adding an agent type needs an entry here, not a code edit.

model_override_rights._doc: An agent's model comes from its definition in ~/.claude/agents. Only the main session (no agent type) may pass `model` to the Agent tool freely; every other spawner needs the exact (spawning type -> requested type -> model) triple listed here. A call without a `model` parameter is always allowed. Granting an exception is an entry here, not a code edit.

build._doc: Read by the orchestrate skill: at most fix_rounds_max fix rounds per task, and the number of independent reviewers per candidate.

_doc_offline: Offline experiment gate (hooks/offline-gate.py + gate_policy.offline_decision). A session named in ~/.claude/offline-sessions.json may not run a command that writes beyond this machine or touches a deployment control plane. denied_heads are refused whatever they do; denied_subcommands name the writing subcommands of a client that is otherwise fine (gh is inverted: only allow_only reads pass, and `gh api` passes until it carries a write flag); db_clients and http_clients are refused only for a host outside local_hosts, HTTP only when the call carries a write method or a body. A name without a dot counts as local.
_doc_bash_clamp: bash-output-clamp hook: for the listed agent types, Bash output goes to a file under $CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR/orch-out and the agent sees head_lines + tail_lines when it exceeds max_bytes.

destructive._doc: deny-destructive hook (gate_policy.destructive_decision). ours = reversible, bounded, project-owned: rm/mv/find -delete/chmod whose every path is under an ours_paths prefix or is the prefix directory itself (tmp, .worktrees, ~/.claude/tmp; the absolute /tmp, ~/Library/Caches and the system temp dir themselves are not ours; entries below the system temp dir are), or lies below a .worktrees directory at any depth (an absolute <repo>/.worktrees/<task> too, not the .worktrees directory itself); paths are judged by their real path (symlinks resolved before each '..'; an rm operand's final component is the object itself unless it is . or .. or ends in /; comma braces expanded); relative paths resolve against the hook's cwd and each top-level cd/pushd (outside { }, blocks, loops, function bodies, pipelines and background jobs, not negated by '!', reached only through '&&', not followed by '||') to a literal directory: for the rest of the command when it is first of its &&/|| chain and the directory exists, else for the rest of its && chain (the directory may be created earlier in it); any other cd makes the directory unknown for the rest of the command, its relative paths not ours; a ( ) or $( ) subshell is its own top level and restores the directory and bindings when it ends; NAME=<literal> and NAME=$(mktemp ...) (a temp-dir path) in the same unconditional position bind $NAME/${NAME} for later segments, any other write to NAME (nested or conditional assignment, +=, declare/local/typeset/export/readonly/unset/read/getopts/for) unbinds it, unbound variables are not ours; git clean / reset --hard / checkout -- <path> / restore whose repository root (nearest .git up from -C or the tracked directory) is a linked worktree below a .worktrees directory or lies under /tmp or the temp dir, and no --work-tree/--git-dir/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_DIR/core.worktree/core.bare in the command; kubectl delete by an ours_labels selector; kubectl writes with a cheap mechanical undo on one object (scale, rollout restart/undo/pause/resume of one object; --all, a selector, several objects or -f/-k ask; the reason names the undo); runs without a prompt. sh/bash/zsh -c strings are classed as the commands they run (a command head that is a variable or a substitution is denied like eval); exec/ssh inner commands have an unknown directory and no variables, a '<' file after kubectl exec -- is read locally as the SQL file; a function whose body runs kubectl ... "$@" is classed as kubectl at each call; kubectl --dry-run before '--' is a read; an unknown kubectl option before the verb asks; chown is always denied. ~/.claude/tools/rm-own [-r] <path>... (the installed or the repository's tool; another script by that name is judged as rm) is class none: it resolves each real path (parent symlinks resolved before '..', the final component not followed) and removes that real path only when this ours rule accepts it, never a .worktrees directory or a repository root, all or nothing; deny reasons for rm/find/mv/chmod/git discards name the allowed alternative. approval = live write whose undo is not mechanical (other kubectl mutations, SQL UPDATE / DELETE ... WHERE via sql_clients): one approval of the plan (the permission prompt, or APPROVE <sha256> where the session cannot prompt), normally per plan script run as `bash <plan>  # DESTRUCTIVE_PLAN sha256=<hex>` from the main session, headers # scope / # undo / # count / # contradiction (may be none) / # prod_position / # way_back, at most plan_max_lines lines and plan_max_bytes bytes, absolute path, no line running another file. A relative mv without '..', variables or globs is a rename and passes unclassed. impossible (no undo) and privileged commands are denied as bare commands (an impossible step runs only from an approved plan; the refusal says so); a command over command_max_bytes is denied unread. Heredoc bodies are data unless they feed a shell, interpreter, ssh/exec or SQL client. ask_in_bypass: whether ask stays ask in bypassPermissions mode (undocumented whether it prompts there); false turns it into deny; a plan is then approved by the owner's prompt line `APPROVE <sha256>` (hooks/plan-approval.py writes approvals_dir/<session_id>/<sha256>, deny-destructive consumes it: one run per approval; agents cannot write approvals_dir: Bash tokens naming it case-folded and normalized, file-tool paths by resolved case-folded path, and any Bash command carrying an APPROVE line are denied; cd-relative paths, shell variables, find -exec, a script file and base64-decoded commands remain open to a deliberate agent only and are accepted as residual).
